description.narrative: Effect of the Program Rate of spread of the disease managed, burden on affected businesses mitigated and poverty contained

By December, doubling rate of COVID-19 confirmed cases is reduced to 20 days or more Progress/Status: As of September 30, the first reporting period of the program, the progress was made to reach the target. The doubling rate of COVID-19 confirmed cases was about 14 days. However, the situation is quickly changing for the worse and by December, it is likely that the virus will be spread more widely than originally expected. Government of Georgia was quick to take decisive measures at the beginning of the pandemic. The government imposed a country-wide lock-down in March, and announced a comprehensive social protection/economic recover package to respond to the crisis. The lock-down and other restrictions led to successful containment of spreading the virus. However, as the restrictions lifted, Georgia saw dramatic increase in cases per day, especially from September.
(Source: Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: IACC and MOILHSA report submitted by September 2020 Actual value:

By December 2020, the number of individuals scoring 0-65,000 on MOILHSA's proxy means testing is retained at 120% of pre-crisis levels. Share of women remains at 55% or lower Progress/Status: For the first reporting period, 391,500 individuals score 0-65,000 in TSA PMT, 55% of whom are women. The progress is in line with the set target for the corresponding indicators. In January 2020, before the COVID-19 pandemic, there were 432 thousand persons (121 thousand households) who were recipients of the cash transfers, which constitutes 11.6% of the whole population. In response to the pandemic, the government decided to expand the coverage. As of September, 2020, around 502 thousand persons receive cash transfers, which is 13.5% of the entire population. Thus, the number of TSA recipients increased by around 16%.
(Source: Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: Report by MOILHSA submitted by December 2020. Actual value:

Output: Enhanced livelihoods support for the most vulnerable segments of the population Indicator: Up to 350,000 workers who are laid off because of COVID-19 (temporarily or permanently) receive temporary unemployment assistance of GEL200 per month for a period of 6 months. Progress/Status: Status: Partially Achieved.
Thus far, the total number of workers who received unemployment assistance of GEL 200 is 161,905 unique individuals. As people lost work at different times, the break-down of the data is as follows: • 50,078 individuals received benefit five times • 31,754 individuals received benefit four times • 22,358 individuals received benefit three times • 29,196 individuals received benefit two times • 28,519 individuals received benefit once.
It is not clear whether the applicants were turned down, or there were not simply that many applicants. Important consideration is to understand whether there will be a deadline for application and people laid off in alter period can also apply. As of September 30, 2020 - GEL 106,288,400 has been spent. (Source: Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 12 Nov 2020) Data Source: MOILHSA submits sex-disaggregated report on number of beneficiaries by December 2020 Actual value:

Indicator: 2 COVID-19 related diagnosis and treatment costs are provided free of charge for people living below the official poverty line to avoid out of pocket payments related to COVID-19 Progress/Status: Status: Target Achieved
As of 10 Sept 2020, All necessary health services related to COVID-19 are supposed to be covered from the basic package of benefits with no out-of-pocket payments regardless of whether patients have medical insurance. (Source: https://www.covid19healthsystem.org/countries/georgia/livinghit.aspx?Section=4.2%20Entitlement%20and%20coverage&Type=Section) COVID-19 related diagnosis and treatment costs are provided free of charge for all people living in Georgia. Approximately 10,000 tests are being done daily. However, the quick increase in the number of COVID-19 cases will likely necessitate even more tests to be administered. (Source: Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 12 Nov 2020) Data Source: Quarterly MOILHSA report

Output: Measures taken to combat the spread of COVID-19 and health sector response capacity strengthened. Indicator: Government publishes a COVID-19 dedicated web page (www.stopcov.ge) which includes detailed information on the list of NPIs adopted by the government to keep the burden on the health system to a minimum. The website includes specific information regarding health protocols for pregnant persons, childbirth and breastfeeding during COVID-19. Progress/Status: Status: Target Achieved.
As of 10 Sep 2020, the government / National Center for Disease Control and Public Health (NCDC) has been working actively with mass media to inform the public about measures put in place. Official advice on hand hygiene, respiratory etiquette, and physical distancing has been issued and disseminated widely starting already in January 2020. Information on outbreak severity and responses are conveyed to the public through mass media and social media and it is updated regularly. The official website for information is https://stopcov.ge/ - the website is available in Georgian, English, Azeri, Armenian and Abkhaz languages, Ossetian is expected to be added soon. In addition to NCDC and Ministry of Internally Displaced Persons from Occupied Territories, Labour, Health and Social Affairs (MoH) websites and it provides governmental institutions as well as the general population with evidence-based information on COVID-19, including risk communication, epidemiological information, control mechanisms, and recommendations for different groups. The website was set up to help prevent COVID-19 in Georgia, soon after the first case was registered on 26 February 2020. (source: https://www.covid19healthsystem.org/countries/georgia/livinghit.aspx?Section=1.1%20Health%20communication&Type=Section) Data Source: Government resolution on containment measures published and content disseminated through social media.
Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Measures taken to combat the spread of COVID-19 and health sector response capacity strengthened. Indicator: MOILHSA provides adequate PPE to all frontline health workers (in sizes suitable for both women and men) Progress/Status: Status: Partially Achieved
As of 10 Sept 2020, all health care workers who may come into direct contact with COVID-19 patients, have been trained according to the WHO guidelines and protocols: the emergency call protocol; rules for safely putting-on/taking-off personal protective equipment; procedures for the transfer of infected persons; and hand and surface treatment with disinfectant solutions. (Source: https://www.covid19healthsystem.org/countries/georgia/livinghit.aspx?Section=2.2%20Workforce&Type=Section) The NCDC management has said that the government has purchased enough tests, both PCR and high quality quick antigen-based tests. So there shouldn't be a problem in delivering the adequate number of COVID-19 tests. Similarly, enough Personal Perfection Equipment was provided to medical workers to ensure safety when treating the patients. However, the data on exact number of PPEs distributed to medical workers has not been provided by relevant agency. (Source: Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 12 Nov 2020) Data Source: MoILHSA report Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y
